I got the impression that the O5 Council tried to erase this office and its occupant from existence, along with all related records, but that it didn't quite take thanks to the strength of the occupant's will to be remembered. Seems the coverup was still successful enough though, since there's no way to know any specifics from this article. It makes me wonder, how much stuff like this is there in the SCPverse that we just don't know about because the Council usually completely succeeds at coverups?

Also, I love that there's Foundation-issue bourbon.

There's a lot of potential here, but I feel like any anomaly capable of comprehending and altering a wide variety of sophisticated legal documents would be a bit more formal and well-spoken.

I certainly won't downvote on that basis, because that's just my personal sense of how an anomaly of this type would behave. Still, ultimately there just wasn't enough weirdness described here to win my upvote. I think the anomaly's main property is sufficiently weird, so a longer and more historically thorough log of its identified historical effects could easily maintain the fun tone while adding more variety.

The extended concern about the earthquake was just not very interesting. It would have been okay as a brief addendum to get the reader to crack a smile one last time, but it went on for far too long; there was no successful development of mounting tension, and the humor of it wore thin quickly.

item.title: Re: Anti-water Bottle (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Not an experienced critter. Take my words with the world's tiniest grain of salt.

+ Koke? Crit?
- NO I HATE KOKE CRIT

*This SCP is about a water bottle that when drunk from will cause the person to experience dehydration.

*It is able to change its appearance depending on location and teleport.

The core anomaly is going to need some work. To me, it feels like you were aware of how uninteresting the first property was and then randomly added the ability to teleport for… what reason? Just for difficult containment? How does it even teleport in the first place? Is it just random? This property just feels like it was added on to inconvenience the Foundation and nothing else. If you can find a way to attach the property to the narrative, you better find a great way to do that, because it just feels very out of place.

After recovery most of the SCP's properties were uncovered except for its ability to teleport. This caused an incident where a higher level researcher was drunk some of the liquid inside, leading to lifelong impairment. SCP was designated Euclid after this incident. A cure for the effects caused by the SCP is still in process.

This just feels like a series of events rather than an actual narrative. A researcher gets dehydrated, the skip becomes Euclid (object classes aren't based on danger, but rather how difficult they are to contain. It would make sense if they found out its teleporting ability, but you've never mentioned how they found out or what they decide to do about it), they try to… find a cure for dehydration? If all the skip does is cause dehydration, I would imagine finding a cure wouldn't be very hard considering we've pretty much already found solutions for it.

These events don't feel like they connect very well to form a clear story. I don't know what I'm supposed to get from this other than "dangerous water bottle cripples researcher, we try to fix it". Maybe you could try shifting the focus onto the researcher and how the water bottle has affected him rather than everything else around him?

Interesting lore that I intend to build on later.

Where is the lore?

I am afraid I may go into uneccessary depth at some point, causing the article to be less intersting/mysterious.

If anything, I'd recommend going even more in-depth. I have no idea where this is going. Mysteries work way better with context, and there's none of that here.

item.title: Re: "When We Didn't Dream" - An SCP Tale Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Hello again! how are you doing?

Thanks for the response, especially the bit about the ending.

The ending definitely does need something more than just lost hope. I like bleak endings, but they only really work when there's a lesson learned, or if it affects more than just the main character. Right now, it seems like the ending doesn't have a payoff and only affects the main character, which thankfully you helped bring to my attention. I think as you recommended, the ending should be bittersweet instead of bleak.
I started to brainstorm a different idea for the ending:
Instead of just all hope being lost and he transforms, The Oneiroi Collective gives him an offer: he can be placed in an endless dream, which would replicate reality completely, with one catch: it takes place only in the summer of 1965, and only in his home town. With no other option, Ty takes the offer, leaving his physical body (which now completely transforms into an instance of the SCP) behind. He falls asleep for the last time.

Of course, I'll probably brainstorm more ending ideas that may work better.

Thanks again for the critique, and I hope you have had a merry Christmas and a great day.

Sincerely, Gravy.

item.title: Re: "When We Didn't Dream" - An SCP Tale Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Hey! How are you doing?

Thank you so much for the response.

The ending is bleak, and I definitely think it could use some work. I'm considering adding something to the ending, to make it bittersweet (like Caspian2 recommended). Instead of Ty just transforming completely, basically making him brain dead, he is offered to order a dream that lasts forever. A dream that replicates real life. However, it will always be the summer of 1965, and his physical body will be completely transformed. With no other option, Ty accepts the offer, and he falls asleep for the last time.
Of course, this is just an idea, and I'll probably brainstorm other endings that might work better.

The reason he knows who The Oneiroi Collective are is more simple. Whenever anyone picks up the phone on SCP-1498, someone claiming to be from The Oneiroi Collective will answer the call.
The reason he finds anomalous abilities is slightly more complex. Ty's main flaw as a character is that he's driven by boredom, and nothing else. All his actions at the beginning of the tale are taken without consideration, as he only takes those actions to relieve himself of boredom. So, when he finds the SCP, although he's at first startled, he eventually becomes enthralled and starts to inspect it, eventually using the phone, in which the main plot begins. He gets addicted to using the SCP not only because it's one of its anomalous abilities, but also because it seems to be a way to escape the boredom of his mind. Of course, he gets more than he bargains for.

Again, thanks for responding. I think I'm going to start writing the draft. When that's finished and edited, I'll submit it to the draft critique forum and probably PM you.

Have a great day, and I hope you had a merry Christmas!

Sincerely, Gravy.

SCP-5415 is a kids toybox that is capable of slowly moving. SCP-5415 is 51 centimeters tall and is 102 centimeters in length.
This object weighs approximately 15.4 kilograms. SCP-5415 is capable of moving approximately 1 meter over a span of 24 hours.

Deleted at -22 and three votes.

The Shadow Door

“Tell me another story.”

“Now now, Abel,” Celwyn said, setting the storybook down on a table and drawing the blanket snug around his son’s shoulders.

“That’s two stories already. Now it’s time for sleep.”

Deleted at -15 and three votes.

SCP-5133 is a golden colored outdoor hot tub with small legs. It appears to be sentient. The wires on the bottom secrete a oily liquid that is highly corrosive to everything except marble. However, the water inside can corrode through everything except for its cover. Its cover should be on at ALL TIMES. The water instantly kills humans on touch. When a human is in its cell, they will feel an urge to touch the water. Tests show it promises to "heal any wound". However, SCP-5133 cannot talk as it has no eyes or mouth. It seems to have a nose on the underside though. It also modifies anything written, typed, or talked about lifting the cover. Bombs have shown to stun the SCP for up to a month (depending on the size).

Deleted at -15 and three votes.

SCP-5134 appears to be a large jar filled with sliced pickles and pickle juice. SCP-5134's lid appears to be a standard pickle jar lid, apart from the fact that no known living being has the strength to remove the lid from the jar. However when any piece of technology such as a prosthetic arm is used to attempt to remove the lid from the jar, the jar is removed with just as much effort as it would take to remove the lid from a non-anomalous pickle jar.

item.title: Dr wondertainment’s instant clown costume (seeking Green Light)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Informative

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is simply cheap plastic packaging held a single red noes, the cardboard label said ‘Dr. Wondertainment’s instant clown costume’ on it. There were no other writing or label on this packaging, no obvious anomalous properties seem to be apparent of the object until placed upon a person.

Central Narrative: Their skin seemed to be rubber now and cloths have morphed to appear goofy and in character of a clown, the face resembles that of a Halloween clown mask creepy and eerie as you stare into its lifeless rubber eyes, and fake rubber teeth, the noes once placed there cannot be removed and causes individuals to wonder mindlessly around room, cities and forests, grabbing onto any item then can use as weapon including knives, hammers, guns and any other blunt object within grasp, so far these entities have only stood menacingly out of view avoiding human contact walking away when approached never using their threatening objects for harmful reasons, and once morning arrives, they disappear.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: upon observation of a deceased victim of SCP-XXXX they find that the noes overtakes a person, turning skin into that of a cheap Halloween mask rubber, their cloths had been effected as well being overtaken by light fabrics like a cheap costume binding to not only frantic but the skin as well much like it was stitching together

Additional Notes: each face is unique and terrifying, no instant of this SCP has taken a life, but all instances have perished either due to fearful reactions of bystanders shooting in self defense, or long term starvation due to the fact an infected individuals loses the will and ability to eat or drink, more research to be conducted.

item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) the Survivors
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: since when did the GOC get space cannons and what do you mean by an alien ship falling from the sky.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is an alien ship that was shot down by the GOC and crashed 20 miles west of San Francisco, pieces of the SCP-XXXX was too badly damaged to know the original shape or size of it.

The name Galactic.Co also appears on multiple occasions on walls and windows, the majority of the SCP-XXXX is a core fueled by large glass containers with a very small amount of SCP-XXXX-2, known as gravitonium.

SCP-XXXX-1 is the Survivors of the incident and appears to be a combination of a human and a orca, they are strong, intelligent and can swim very fast, they were discovered in Hawaii existing their escape pods with a few of them injured, because of the GOC they are stuck here with no way for them to contact their home world.

+ show block
– hide block

They claimed that they’re from the other side of the galaxy testing some new form of hyper drive from Galactic.Co, the only problem is that it needs larger amounts of SCP-XXXX-2, they thought that there’s enough to go here and back but when they got here, the glass container was almost completely empty.

As for project space cannon, the GOC was building it after the interaction with SCP-2845, knowing that SCP-2845 came from space they decided that earth needed a defense against all extraterrestrial anomalies and entities.

They started the project 7 months later after the foundation contained SCP-2845 and finished it 4 years later with the help of Anderson’s Robotics.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: the hook here is about how the foundation is supposed to take control of the space cannon program from the GOC and the problem with fragments of the ship being used by civilians and groups of interest, like Anderson’s Robotics experimenting with SCP-XXXX-2 or the chaos Insurgency using it as a powerful weapon/bomb.

Additional Notes: this SCP idea is split up in 2 forms, 1 being about the SCP itself and 1 about Project Space Cannon and why the GOC built it, there is also going to be a series of events that took place in the ship before its doom, the trouble of keeping this from the public and a series of test involving SCP-XXXX-2.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Re: Idea Critique: Joke SCP: Cognitohazard
item.content:encoded:
I agree — writing style and details are ingredients, but never the finishing potion for a functioning joke SCP. The thing with joke SCPs and merely comedic mainlist SCPs are that the former tends to have a single punchline — of course, timing is crucial, too. Reveal it too early and you might already give away the joke. Drag it on for too long and people may just click off prematurely.

The thing is: as I had said, humor is subjective. The wiki votes on it, so whether it survives or not, mostly depends on their personal tastes. Everyone's probably got their own specific set of funni jokes, but to pull something like a joke SCP, or rather, basically any posted work, one should be aware of how the majority receives that joke. Without elaboration on the anomaly, I'm not sure how it's going to set up an escalation up until that climax, and hence see if it can work as a -J.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Idea Critique: Joke SCP: Cognitohazard

item.title: Re: Idea Critique: Joke SCP: Cognitohazard
item.content:encoded:
Joke SCPs also tend to rely heavily on writing style and the fine details. I could see this working, but it would definitely need buildup to work. Jokes are about timing and delivery, not really how objectively funny a punchline is.

item.title: Re: Idea Critique: Joke SCP: Cognitohazard
item.content:encoded:
Hi, just a casual, pitching in with my two cents.

Joke articles need a punchline — this doesn't seem like one, and even if it is meant to be one, I don't think that statement may merit comedic appeal, personally. In fact, there's no elaboration on what the anomaly even does other than outright say it's "cognitohazardous". What does the anomaly do? How does it build-up to the punchline?

I've seen joke SCPs — humor is a relatively subjective matter: some may like it, some won't. So, it's… difficult, maybe perhaps even more tedious than a regular SCP article to really make it funny, while also fulfilling the benchmark of what most of the wiki tends to see as "funny".

item.title: A Wholesome Gift
item.content:encoded:
Sandbox link, clocking in at around 2k words.

+ Spoilers?
- Close

The main plot follows the story of Xasbo, a guy who adores cats, until at one of the festivals, he unknowingly consumes his own cat in part due to a tradition in some parts of China which practise the culture of eating cat meat, leading to his disillusionment. The practice itself isn't widely practised, and it's more centered within the Guangdong and Guangxi provinces, so the latter was the first pick of where the massacre happened. After the villagers die, the place somehow got the anomalous power to serve as a place for housing cats.

You can probably say he's more of the extreme of the extreme, PETA activist who cares nothing for humankind.

Main concerns are SPaG, whether the interview is a huge exposition dump, whether Xasbo's personality can mirror more of a subtly psychopathic character, and whether it ends on a sufficiently spooky note in contrast to Xasbo's view of a literal massacre as a festive occasion for the cats.

item.title: Re: HOT SIRENS IN YOUR AREA - Greenlights needed!
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the crit! I appreciate the in-depth-ness.

+ show block
– hide block

In answer to the questions:

Why do these ads exist?

I’ve been pondering over this specific part of the question for a while now, and it occurs to me that I didn’t ever really think through why they’d use ads specifically. I think that, in the end, it would probably be because spam ads specifically would blend in pretty well.

Is there a number?

…uh, oops.
Yeah, I didn’t consider that. I think that once I revise this concept, it would probably be better that the ads are like those pop-up ones that just display a big flashy image and some sound, instead of a phone number or text.

And about your suggestions:

A Love story

Goddamnit, you beat me to it.
After the comments about the murder monster stuff, I had been personally considering reworking the story from being a coven of human-eating sirens into it being a single siren who’s just really lonely. Instead of the ads bringing the siren to the victim, the ads would induce an anomalous effect that caused the victim to go towards the siren instead. This affect would be triggered by the ad’s music just straight-up being the siren’s song.

Still not sure what the siren would do to them once they arrived. Maybe it would just get them to bring it food and make them listen to its song for a while. That’d be nice.

Not strictly a love story, but I’m usually better at writing emotional things over horror, so this could have a lot more potential.

To clarify, I will definitely be making a very large amount of changes before I try and redraft this concept, which is why some questions didn’t get answered- a lot of what you (and a few others in this thread) made me realise that I didn’t actually think a lot of these concepts through before I posted this. Beginner’s mistake.

Once again, thank you very much! I greatly appreciate the feedback.

item.title: The Flight of the Koalas
item.content:encoded:
Word Count: 2,371

Link: http://scpdsandbox.wikidot.com/veraltanic-page-3-0

Hello everyone! This is Veralta once again completing a draft that I hope to publish as a New Year's gift! I have written a social commentary about koalas, how they and the aboriginal Australians have been affected by the bushland fires, and how people should be more ecologically-minded. I also featured a trip throughout Australia's rich culture and locations, with several of the article's parts being based on Dreamtime1 lore.

Note: I have tried to make the parts of the article that I have based on Dreamtime to be as least abstract as possible, and clear. If there are questions or ambiguity that you can find about them, feel free to mention it in the critique!

Here are the points that I want to be reviewed:

1. Is the pacing and narrative good enough?
2. Is the worldbuilding and attention to detail decent and palatable?
3. Does it sound too preachy?
4. If applicable, have you noticed several problems and contradictions with Dreamtime lore and aboriginal beliefs?2

All in all, I hope you enjoy this SCP in time for the New Year (and a new leaf for all of us)! Thank you to those who will review this!

Footnotes
1. Umbrella term for aboriginal Australian beliefs.
2. I have researched this part as much as possible, so I would like to not screw up something here.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: The Architects Automaton
item.content:encoded:
An Automaton of unknown origin, inexplicably in operational condition. Creates increasingly complex geometric patterns that grab the eye and boggle the mind.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Cosmic Horror

Elevator Pitch:
SCP-XXXX is a functional Automaton, appearing to be from the 1800s. It resembles a small child writing at a desk, to which it is attached. Upon supplying SCP-XXXX with paper and ink for the attached pen and turning the crank, the crank will lock in place. However, it has been discovered through intense physical manipulation and scientific reasoning, that SCP-XXXX will respond to particular audio frequencies, all of which are outside the audible spectrum. It will then activate autonomously and begin drawing with extreme precision until its internal potential energy is exhausted.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:
The story laying under the surface of this strange artifact as well as many others that will come is the story of the Architect. A person from an unknown time and place that has found a way to harness mathematics and geometry into a form of literal magic. Though the Architect's whereabouts and physicality are yet unknown, there are many strange, otherworldly objects that lend themselves to prove his existence.

Associate SCP concepts-
- The architect’s Automaton Known
- The arithmetic sigils (x3) Unknown
- The Arithmicon Unknown
- The huntsmen Unknown
- The Lead Knights Unknown
- The Tide Unknown
- The face of god Unknown
- The seed of Eden Unknown
- The black moor Unknown
- The eye of Yog Unknown
- The traveler's cube Unknown

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
The drawings it produces vary wildly dependent on the frequency given to it and will grow in complexity with each subsequent process. It has been noted that attempting to investigate and calculate these geometric patterns will result in Dissociative Amnesia, Psychosis, Dementia, Alzheimer's syndrome, and many other effects. This is seemingly at random, and no two cases are alike but in one distinct factor. Each of the subjects exposed to the drawings seems to experience delusions and dreams of a masked figure cloaked in black.

Additional Notes:
It is not yet known what happens when SCP-XXXX is allowed to finish one of its patterns, but it is certainly best left to conjecture.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Re: Imaginary Friends (Greenlight Wanted)
item.content:encoded:
While I do like the core concept you're going for, the SCP itself feels like a deviation of a particular cartoon. While that's not necessarily a bad thing, you DID put your own spin on it after all, but for me, I think it's a bit way too similar to said cartoon to the point readers might just see this as a rip-off, or that it's lacking originality.

What does catch my attention is how you're trying to show the more sympathetic and kind side of the Foundation, so I suggest you keep that story intact if you decide to refine the SCP. If I were to come up with this concept, it would be that the "imaginary friends" are actually interdimensional parasites that only feed on children.

Moving on, your English might need some improvement if you're gonna try to write in a clinical tone. I'm not saying you're barely understandable, your English is good enough for normal conversations and you did explain your concept well, but a little bit of studying and improvement can never hurt and will only make your writing even better.
